summary.text: Eldest daughter of Acessamenus with whom wide-flowing Axius lay and begat Pelegon — distinct from Periboea wife of Oeneus, Penelope's mother, and the Phaeacian nymph.

story.text: Homer names Periboea only through her son's boast: Asteropaeus, son of Pelegon, was begotten of wide-flowing Axius and Periboea, eldest of the daughters of Acessamenus, when the deep-eddying River lay with her.
